original_description: Sets the maintainer's standard for writing and reviewing committed Go tests (_test.go): the golden hierarchy of contract authority, go-doc-first design and review, Go-team snippets to imitate, references per scenario.
best_description: Sets the maintainer's standard for writing and reviewing committed Go tests (_test.go): the golden hierarchy of contract authority, go-doc-first design and review, Go-team snippets to imitate, references per scenario.
final_description: Go tests, at every stage: write or generate a package's `_test.go`; review or critique tests someone else wrote; rework a suite that tests one exported symbol at a time or pokes at internals; turn thin assertions into runnable Examples for pkgsite; build a conformance / `httptest`-style testing package so outside implementers can prove they conform; shape an API up front so its tests stay writable. Reach for it too when finishing any Go code, since committed code without contract tests is unfinished. Applies the maintainer's standard: tests state the package's contract with its users, drafted from the exported docs before the source, plain-English property names, one package-level suite over per-symbol tests, a mandatory representative example, typed errors over string matching, and a hard-to-write test read as a redesign signal. Not for non-Go suites, `go vet` or fuzz triage, test-plan documents, or explaining stdlib testing APIs.

history.description: Use when Go tests are in play: writing or generating `_test.go` files for a package, reviewing or critiquing someone's tests, reworking a bad suite, turning assertions into runnable examples for pkgsite, building a conformance/`httptest`-style testing package for third-party implementers, or shaping an API up front so it stays testable. Also load before finishing any Go code-writing task, since committed code needs contract tests. Applies the maintainer's standard: tests state the package's contract with its users, drafted from the exported docs first; one package-level unit rather than one test per exported symbol; plain-English property names; mandatory representative example; typed errors over string matching; a test that's hard to write means the API needs redesign. Not for non-Go test suites, CI flakiness in other stacks, `go vet`/fuzz triage, or test-plan documents.
